subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message sender identity contract for multi-agent conversations, and what canonical fields and trust semantics should flow through protocol, transcripts, live/history events, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: The remaining work affects public Gateway APIs, persisted transcript/session semantics, UI rendering, and multi-agent trust boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent contract shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Additive Identity Contract
options.body: Introduce one canonical sender identity object and migrate the existing provenance, senderLabel, and avatar/grouping paths to consume it while preserving compatibility.

options.title: Continue Narrow Fixes Only
options.body: Keep handling specific regressions such as requester prompt names or empty-label fallbacks without committing to a broad identity contract yet.

options.title: Defer To Multi-Agent Model
options.body: Leave this open until multi-agent conversation permissions and UI architecture are ready to own sender identity end to end.

recommendation.title: Design Additive Identity Contract
recommendation.body: Introduce one canonical sender identity object and migrate the existing provenance, senderLabel, and avatar/grouping paths to consume it while preserving compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and history both point to steipete as the closest owner for provenance/session contracts and multi-agent UX direction.
